newsitem.title: BELARUS: Possible compromise in Belarus crisis - source says.
newsitem.headline: Possible compromise in Belarus crisis - source says.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko has said he is ready to compromise with his opponents over plans for a controversial referendum to increase his powers, a senior Belarussian political source said on Tuesday.

The source said Lukashenko made his offer in a meeting with Valery Tikhinya, president of the Constitutional Court. "It seems that Lukashenko is ready to withdraw his constitutional draft and there will be no impeachment today. But let's see what happens tomorrow," the source said.
The hint of a compromise from Lukashenko came after a day of mounting alarm among neighbouring states at the confrontation between the hardline president and his parliament.
Lukashenko has ignored the current constitution and rulings by the Constitutional Court in declaring that the referendum, for which voting has already started, must be binding.
It was not clear if the 42-year-old president was prepared to drop the referendum altogether or modify his position on how it should be implemented. Parliament on Tuesday began steps to impeach him.
Other political sources in Minsk said the republic's foreign ministry had written to Lukashenko's security council urging that he tone down his hostile rhetoric against the West.
